results.claim: ELLSA runs a single interleaved sequence on a fixed 1-second time block with the order speech -> image -> text -> action: `<bos>{5 speech embeddings}<eos><boi>{image tokens}<eoi><bot>{8 text tokens / <silence>}<eot><boa>{FAST action tokens / dummy action tokens}<eoa>`; rate mismatch is handled purely by fixed slots plus explicit idle tokens (<silence>, dummy actions). Two 8B experts need 786-854 ms per 1 s block on an A100; a 0.48 s block halves latency but the action expert loses 10-13 points because shorter action sequences 'reduce the temporal coherence of the generated actions'.
results.evidence_quote: "In general, ELLSA operates on a one-second time block, within which it processes one second of speech input and a single video frame, generates eight tokens of text output (or a single <silence> token when no verbal response is required), and produces one second of speech and action output." ... "Both modes follow the same modality order, speech → image → text → action. In speech-only mode, the visual input between <boi> and <eoi> is absent, and the model consistently produces dummy actions without actual movement." ... Default mode: "<bos> {5 speech embeddings} <eos> <boi> {front view image tokens} <eoi> <boi> {gripper view image tokens} <eoi> <bot> {8 text tokens / <silence>} <eot> <boa> {action tokens / dummy action tokens} <eoa>" ... "The LLM backbone is LLama-3.1-8B-Instruct" / "The backbone is Emu3-Base, the final 1,024 token IDs of which are replaced with FAST tokens" / "The LLM backbone of the speech expert (LLaMA-3.1-Instruct) and that of the action expert (Emu3-Base) share identical configurations: 32 transformer layers, a hidden size of 4096, 32 attention heads" ... Appendix G.1: "a speech expert that generates 4 text tokens every 0.48 s and an action expert that produces 5 action frames per block. ... the action expert exhibits a notable degradation. This drop is likely due to the shorter action sequences, which can reduce the temporal coherence of the generated actions." ... "we report the average per–time-block latency measured on an A100 GPU"; Table 9(b): 1s SPATIAL 95.4% OBJECT 98.8% GOAL 93.6% LONG 94.0%; 0.48s 91.0% 92.4% 84.2% 81.0%; Table 9(d): 1s 854ms / 786ms; 0.48s 455ms / 428ms.
results.correction: Two details are off. (1) The action-expert loss at 0.48 s is 4.4–13.0 points depending on suite, not '10–13': SPATIAL 95.4→91.0 (−4.4), OBJECT 98.8→92.4 (−6.4), GOAL 93.6→84.2 (−9.4), LONG 94.0→81.0 (−13.0); the composed SA-MoE drops 9.8/10.8/13.0/12.8 (SPATIAL 90.8→81.0, OBJECT 95.8→85.0, GOAL 86.4→73.4, LONG 84.4→71.6). (2) The paper's default-mode template has two image segments per block in LIBERO (`<boi>{front view}<eoi><boi>{gripper view}<eoi>`), which the claim collapses to one `{image tokens}` slot. Everything else holds: 1 s block, speech→image→text→action order, 5 speech embeddings (25 Hz→5 Hz), 8 text tokens or `<silence>`, FAST action tokens or dummy actions, A100 latency 854/786 ms at 1 s and 455/428 ms at 0.48 s, and the verbatim 'reduce the temporal coherence' explanation. 'Two 8B experts' is a fair paraphrase: the paper names LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct and Emu3-Base (never says '8B' for Emu3) but states both share an identical 32-layer/4096-hidden/32-head configuration.

results.claim: DuplexSLA decodes user audio, assistant speech and a rate-limited textual 'action channel' on one shared 160 ms chunk clock inside a single token stream: `<|user_audio_begin|> U U <|user_audio_end|> <|assistant_audio_begin|> T A A A A <|assistant_audio_end|> {<=10 action tokens} <|action_end|>`. Idle chunks emit <vad_silence>/<tts_pad> anchors and always the <|action_end|> marker ('keeps every chunk strictly aligned to the 160 ms clock'); the <=10-token cap is 'a deployment budget, not an architectural constraint' chosen so decoding fits the chunk on the accelerator, and overflow spills FIFO into later chunks without splitting a tool-call block or blocking speech.
results.evidence_quote: "Let Δ=160 ms be the chunk size on the conversational clock" ... per-chunk layout "<|user_audio_begin|> UU <|user_audio_end|> / <|assistant_audio_begin|> T AAAA <|assistant_audio_end|> / ⟨action text⟩ <|action_end|>" ... "Whenever the chunk has nothing to say, T is predicted as a special anchor token (<vad_silence> or <tts_pad>) and the four A tokens are predicted as the corresponding silence audio codes. The <|action_end|> marker terminates the chunk regardless of whether any action text was emitted, which keeps every chunk strictly aligned to the 160 ms clock." ... §2.3: "Real-time full-duplex interaction requires the per-chunk decoding cost of the model to fit inside one 160 ms chunk on the actual inference hardware. After the assistant TA4 unit is paid for, the autoregressive decoding throughput of a 7B-scale backbone on mainstream inference accelerators leaves room for only a small number of action-channel tokens per chunk. We therefore cap the action channel at 10 text tokens per chunk, with a safe margin against the per-chunk wall-clock budget; tokens that do not fit spill into the action segments of the following chunks. This bound is a deployment budget, not an architectural constraint, and can be re-tuned per accelerator without retraining." ... §3.3: "turns the action stream into a single FIFO queue keyed by trigger time ... If an action's planning text plus tool-call body exceeds the per-chunk ≤ 10-token budget, the surplus tokens spill into the action segments of the following chunks. Any later-triggered action waits in the queue until the in-flight action has fully drained ... it never preempts an earlier action, and never breaks an open <|toolcall_begin|> . . . <|toolcall_end|> block." ... "this FIFO queue on the action channel never blocks assistant speech" ... Table: "Backbone scale: 7B speech-LM, initialized from Step-Audio 2 mini"; "DuplexSLA is initialized from Step-Audio 2 mini [20], a 7B-scale audio language model."
results.correction: None to the claim as written. Confirmed from the PDF text that the backbone is 7B ('7B speech-LM, initialized from Step-Audio 2 mini'); the '77B' seen in HTML summaries is a parse artifact. Turn-taking numbers (normal 96.00%/0.27 s, pause 93.33%/0.27 s, interrupt 99.33%/0.40 s, backchannel 98.33%/0.32 s), tool calling 85.56%/0.64 s vs cascade 91.33%/2.77 s, and the 2-chunk (320 ms) user-transcript lag are also confirmed.

results.claim: Moshi reconciles ~3-4 text tokens/s with 12.5 Hz audio by padding the text stream with PAD/EPAD tokens (about 65 % of text slots) and decoding 17 parallel streams per 80 ms frame (1 text + 8 own audio + 8 user audio) with a 7B Temporal Transformer plus a small Depth Transformer; inter-stream delays are the control knob: acoustic delay 2 frames in pretraining and 1 in fine-tuning (160 ms theoretical latency), text delay 0 for dialogue, and a 2 s text or audio delay turns the same model into streaming ASR or TTS.
results.evidence_quote: "a sample of English speech can be represented with around 3 to 4 text tokens per second." ... "two special tokens: PAD and EPAD, that never appear in any of the word tokens" ... "In English conversational speech, we observe that padding tokens represent about 65% of the tokens." ... "amounting to a total number of K = 2Q + 1 streams, with Q = 8 in the experiments." ... "Mimi's encoder projects a 24kHz waveform to a latent representation of 12.5 frames per second"; "Both its initial frame size and overall stride correspond to 80ms" ... "Helium, a 7B-parameter text LLM"; "our Depth Transformer has 6 layers, a dimension of 1024" ... Table 1: "Acoustic delay – 2 1 1 1 / Text delay – ±0.6 0 0 0" ... "As described in Table 1, we pretrain Moshi with an acoustic delay of 2 and finetune it with an acoustic delay of 1, for a theoretical latency of 160ms." ... §5.7: "we train a streaming TTS model by delaying audio tokens by 2 seconds, giving some lookahead to the text tokens, and teacher forcing text tokens at inference. Similarly, we train a streaming ASR model by delaying text tokens by 2 seconds, allowing the model to listen to audio content before generating text tokens." ... Abstract: "a theoretical latency of 160ms, 200ms in practice".
results.correction: None to the claim text. Two notes on the numbers field only: the delay-pattern/RQ-Transformer perplexity ablation ([0,2,2,2,2,2,2,2]+RQ 36.8 vs [0,1..7]+RQ 40.3 vs [0,2,...] no-RQ 135.4) is Table 5 in the paper, not Table 6; and the paper states '200ms in practice' without naming an L4 GPU anywhere in its text (the L4 figure comes from Kyutai's release materials, not this paper).

results.claim: Real-Time Chunking makes chunked policies robust to inference delay by freezing the first d = floor(delta/dt) actions of the next chunk and inpainting the rest via guidance; with pi0.5 at 50 Hz (H = 50) and d up to 16 (320 ms) real bimanual tasks show 'no degradation, whereas synchronous degrades linearly', at +21 ms overhead.
results.evidence_quote: "We define d:=⌊δ/Δt⌋ and call this quantity the inference delay, corresponding to number of controller timesteps between when o_t is received and when A_t is available." ... "The first d actions from the new chunk cannot be used, since those timesteps will have already passed by the time the new chunk becomes available. Thus, it makes sense to 'freeze' those actions to the values that we know will be executed; our goal is then to fill in the remainder of the new chunk in a way that is consistent with this frozen prefix." ... "The first d actions get a weight of 1; the last s actions of the new chunk do not overlap with the previous chunk, so they get a weight of 0; the actions in between get weights that exponentially decay from 1 to 0." ... Real-world: "We use π0.5 (H=50, Δt=20ms) with n=5 denoising steps"; "We use remote inference over LAN, which adds 10-20ms of latency, giving a starting inference delay around d≈6 for RTC"; "we also evaluate all methods with +100ms and +200ms of injected latency, corresponding to d≈11 and d≈16, respectively"; "giving a model latency of 76ms for the baselines and 97ms for RTC"; "RTC is completely robust to injected delay, showing no degradation, whereas synchronous degrades linearly and both TE variants do not run at all due to causing such high oscillations that the robot's protective stop is triggered."
results.correction: None. All numbers match: d=⌊δ/Δt⌋, π0.5 at Δt=20 ms (50 Hz) with H=50, d≈16 at +200 ms injected (≈320 ms total including ~6 steps of base LAN/inference delay), 97 − 76 = 21 ms overhead on an RTX 4090, and the quoted sentence appears in the real-world bimanual results (6 tasks; 12 Kinetix tasks in sim).

sweeps.topic: Non-RGB tokenization for transformer navigation policies: LiDAR/BEV/occupancy map tokens, audio and speech event tokens, and structured goal/plan/user state tokens - token budgets, encoders, and measured effects on success

findings.claim: In a navigation transformer that tokenizes LiDAR (PointTransformerV3 -> polar sector-ring grid -> K GeM-pooled tokens) alongside RGB tokens, a 1-token MLP goal and a 1-token MLP embodiment, masking the LiDAR tokens costs about half the success rate while masking images costs 10-30%; the full model beats the RGB-only NoMaD baseline 85% vs 15% on a real robot.
findings.source_title: ViLiNT: Multimodal embodiment-aware navigation transformer
findings.kind: arXiv preprint (full text read at arxiv.org/html/2604.19267), CC BY 4.0
findings.numbers: Sim SR (100 trials/env): full 0.79/0.61/0.76; LiDAR masked 0.17/0.37/0.20; image masked 0.72/0.67/0.23; NoMaD-FT 0.33/0.37/0.12; '166% increase in SR and 62% reduction in CR'; real Husky + Ouster OS1-32: 85% vs 15%; sequence length S=(C+1)+K+2; 2x body-size token makes robot refuse corridors < 1.5*max(w,l)
findings.relevance: Direct evidence that the Mid-360 should feed Model A's 10 Hz loop as LiDAR tokens, and that goal and body-size priors can each be a single MLP token.

findings.claim: A transformer over 360-degree LiDAR ray tokens (180 rays x 15 history frames, from a 30x180 spherical depth image) plus proprioception runs at 50 Hz in ~1.3 ms on a Unitree Go2 with Livox Mid-360 and Jetson AGX Orin 64 GB, beside PPO locomotion, safety-shield and navigation policies, with zero real-world collisions.
findings.source_title: REASAN: Learning Reactive Safe Navigation for Legged Robots
findings.kind: arXiv preprint (full text read at arxiv.org/html/2512.09537)
findings.numbers: 180 equidistant rays, 2-degree spherical downsampling -> 30x180 depth image, 15 frames; all modules 50 Hz, estimator ~1.3 ms/cycle; training 4h/15h/7h/10h (12 GB VRAM); sim SR ScaSparse 91.1+-1.9%, ScaDense 79.1+-4.4%, Maze 95.2+-2.9%, DyMaze 68.2+-2.3%, Hold 65.8+-3.4%; real runs 270 s / 180 s / 190 s / 93 s with zero collisions; LSTM(256)+MLP(512-256-128)+1D-CNN(64)
findings.relevance: Same hardware as Parcel; proves a LiDAR token transformer fits the 10 Hz act-token budget with headroom.

findings.claim: For VLM-based navigators, a raw obstacle/occupancy map image is worth nothing, but an annotated semantic map (text labels at region centroids) rendered as one SigLIP image replaces the whole frame history: SR rises from 27.3 (no map) to 36.5, memory is a constant 0.17 MB instead of 276 MB at 300 steps, and inference drops 79.5%.
findings.source_title: MapNav: A Novel Memory Representation via Annotated Semantic Maps for VLM-based Vision-and-Language Navigation
findings.kind: ACL 2025 paper (full text read at arxiv.org/html/2502.13451v5)
findings.numbers: R2R-CE val unseen ablation: no map SR 27.3/SPL 23.2; plain top-down map 26.4/21.9; semantic map w/o labels 29.1/24.5; annotated ASM 36.5/34.3; ASM+current+2 history 39.7/37.2 vs NaVid all-frames 37.4/35.9; RxR-CE zero-shot 32.6/27.7 vs 23.8/21.2; inference 0.25 s vs 1.22 s; memory 0.17 MB constant vs 276 MB; backbone LLaVA-OneVision (SigLIP-so400m-384, Qwen2-7B)
findings.relevance: Tells Model A's slow lane to consume the LiDAR occupancy grid as an annotated image, not as geometry or text.

findings.claim: Direct speech tokens (Whisper encoder -> ~300 tokens per utterance projected into the LLM) match text instructions and beat an ASR cascade by 5-18 points on chained manipulation tasks, and the speaker's voice enables owner-specific tasks at 86.5% vs 19.2% for a text VLA.
findings.source_title: VLAS: Vision-Language-Action Model With Speech Instructions For Customized Robot Manipulation
findings.kind: ICLR 2025 paper (full text read at arxiv.org/html/2502.13508)
findings.numbers: Whisper: 80-bin mel padded to 3000 frames -> 1500 states -> /5 -> MLP (~300 speech tokens); CALVIN LH-1..5: text VLA 95.5/85.0/74.9/66.8/58.2, VLAS speech 94.2/84.0/73.2/64.3/54.6, real speech 93.6/82.8/71.6/61.4/51.3, VLA+ASR 88.7/74.1/61.0/49.2/40.2; customization VLAS 86.5% (real speech 78.6%) vs text VLA 19.2% vs no-RAG 16.0%; SQA 185K samples/1,152 voices; CSI ~194K clips
findings.relevance: Model B should carry an owner-voice embedding as a persistent user token and pass speech, not only ASR text, when identity matters.

findings.claim: The only measured real-robot audio navigation transfer predicts a 9x9 top-down acoustic field from one second of binaural audio plus a 128x128 depth image and hands the peak to a waypoint planner; it reached 75% real-world success while the end-to-end RL policy failed every real trial.
findings.source_title: Sim2Real Transfer for Audio-Visual Navigation with Frequency-Adaptive Acoustic Field Prediction
findings.kind: IROS 2024 paper (arXiv PDF read via local pdftotext; project page also read)
findings.numbers: Sim continuous AudioGoal: AFP SR 0.91/SPL 0.76; AFP w/o vision 0.84/0.71; DDPPO 0.82/0.63; Direction Follower 0.67/0.50; Gan et al. 0.63/0.53; Random 0.01; real Hello Robot + 3Dio binaural mic: 20 episodes, 75% success; DDPPO 0/20; field L=9; using all frequencies gives 0.86 m error vs best band
findings.relevance: Audio events should enter Model A as a local field or bearing token, not as raw audio into the act-token policy.

findings.claim: A navigation foundation model deployed on a Unitree Go2 holds all observations to a fixed 1600-token budget (64 tokens for the latest frame, 4 per history frame, exponential-decay temporal sampling) and injects camera azimuth and time as dedicated sinusoidal identifier tokens; it still needs a remote RTX 4090 and 0.5 s per 8-waypoint trajectory.
findings.source_title: Embodied Navigation Foundation Model (NavFoM)
findings.kind: arXiv preprint (full text read at arxiv.org/html/2509.12129), CC BY 4.0
findings.numbers: 1600-token nav budget (2048 in experiments); 64 tok latest frame, 4 tok/history frame; BATS keep prob P(t)=(1-eps)e^{k(t-T)/T}+eps, eps=0.1; Qwen2-7B + DINOv2 + SigLIP; 12.7M samples (VLN 3.37M, objnav 1.02M, tracking 897K, driving 681K, web 2.03M, QA 4.76M); R2R-CE SR 61.7/SPL 55.3; RxR-CE 64.4/56.2; HM3D-OVON 45.2; EVT-Bench 88.4; 0.5 s on RTX 4090; 110 real cases
findings.relevance: Sets the token budget and the identifier-token pattern for pose/time state in Model A's slow lane.

findings.claim: Structured navigation state can be tokenized per entity for a frozen 7B LLM: each frontier/object token = MLP(coordinates) + MLP(geodesic distance) + DINOv2 visual feature + CLIP-text(category) + learnable type vector, and each past position one path token, totalling about 200 tokens (5 frontiers + 100 objects + 50 path) - half of Uni-NaVid - with state-of-the-art object-nav success.
findings.source_title: FOM-Nav: Frontier-Object Maps for Object Goal Navigation
findings.kind: arXiv preprint (full text read at arxiv.org/html/2512.01009v1)
findings.numbers: ~200 tokens; LLaVA-1.6-7B frozen, D=4096; HM3D v2 SR 75.8/SPL 47.9 (VLFM 64.0/33.0); HM3D v1 73.0/52.1; MP3D 44.6/23.9; tokens w/o visual features 63.7/38.2; local frontier mask +5.3 SR; 760k training steps; real TIAGo++: map update 130 ms, LLaVA forward 100 ms on RTX 4060, 20 GB GPU
findings.relevance: Recipe for goal-bearing/distance and candidate-target tokens that the plan lane can hand to the act-token loop.

findings.claim: Dense feature grids in the policy transformer help, but plain semantic maps barely do: on R2R-CE val unseen, no map 45.19 SR, top-down semantic map 46.36, object-feature map 47.61, GridMM feature grid 49.05; map scale 8x8 -> 14x14 -> 20x20 gives 47.07 -> 49.05 -> 49.86 SR, and egocentric relative coordinates beat absolute ones.
findings.source_title: GridMM: Grid Memory Map for Vision-and-Language Navigation
findings.kind: ICCV 2023 paper (arXiv PDF read via local pdftotext)
findings.numbers: Default 14x14 = 196 map tokens, CLIP ViT-B/16 grid features, instruction-relevance aggregation; Table 5: no map 45.19/37.82, DUET topo 47.02/38.86, semantic map 46.36/38.41, object features 47.61/40.13, GridMM 49.05/40.99; Table 7: 8x8 47.07/39.49, 14x14 49.05/40.99, 20x20 49.86/42.52; absolute coords 48.72 vs ego 49.05; R2R-CE test unseen SR 46/SPL 39
findings.relevance: Sizes the map-token grid (~200 tokens) if occupancy ever enters the trained policy rather than the VLM.

findings.claim: A 21x21-cell, 0.5 m metric map (441 cell tokens, 15.2 GFLOPs in the short-term transformer) is the sweet spot for map tokens: 11x11 at 0.5 m gives SR 73.27 for 4.5 GFLOPs, 21x21 gives 74.88 for 15.2 GFLOPs, and 31x31 gives 74.84 for 32.7 GFLOPs.
findings.source_title: BEVBert: Multimodal Map Pre-training for Language-guided Navigation
findings.kind: ICCV 2023 paper (arXiv PDF read via local pdftotext)
findings.numbers: Table 7 (R2R val unseen): 11x11/0.5m 4.5G SR 73.27 SPL 63.07; 11x11/1.0m 4.5G 74.58/63.37; 21x21/0.5m 15.2G 74.88/63.60; 31x31/0.5m 32.7G 74.84/64.88; map 10.5 m square; abstract: 73 SR R2R test, 59 SR R2R-CE test, 54.2 SDTW RxR; +4 SR/+2 SPL over ETPNav on R2R-CE; RxR val unseen SR 68.5
findings.relevance: Prices map-token count against FLOPs for Parcel's Orin budget.

findings.claim: Feeding a top-view map image with text boxes and a coordinate grid to Qwen2.5-VL-7B raises zero-shot object-nav SR from 45.0 (language-only reasoning) to 52.0; removing text boxes drops it back to 45.0 and removing the coordinate grid to 46.0, while removing the obstacle layer costs only 3 points.
findings.source_title: TopV-Nav: Unlocking the Top-View Spatial Reasoning Potential of MLLM for Zero-shot Object Navigation
findings.kind: arXiv preprint (PDF read via local pdftotext)
findings.numbers: Map 1000x1000 px at 20 px/m; HM3D subset: baseline 45.0/25.44, +map 49.0/28.07, +DMS 50.0/27.16, +PTD 52.0/28.73; w/o history 51.0, w/o obstacle 49.0/26.88, w/o text boxes 45.0/26.16, w/o coordinate grid 46.0/26.08; MLLM: LLaVA-NeXT-8B 50.0, Qwen2.5-VL-7B 52.0, GPT-4o 53.0; main MP3D 35.2/16.4, HM3D 52.0/28.6
findings.relevance: Second independent measurement that labels and coordinate references, not occupancy pixels, are what a VLM extracts from a map.

findings.claim: Occupancy prediction as an auxiliary head on a voxel token grid is a measured lever: adding the volume state raises REVERIE SR 52.31 -> 55.98 and R2R 72.71 -> 75.80; occupancy supervision alone gives R2R SR 74.90 and all three 3D tasks 75.80 (about +3 SR / +4 SPL on R2R test).
findings.source_title: Volumetric Environment Representation for Vision-Language Navigation (VER)
findings.kind: CVPR 2024 paper (arXiv PDF read via local pdftotext)
findings.numbers: Multi-resolution occupancy labels 0.4 m and 0.2 m; >50 billion annotated voxels; Table 4: w/o volume state 52.31/34.91 (REVERIE), 72.71/61.13 (R2R); full 55.98/39.66, 75.80/65.37; Table 8: occ only 74.90/63.82, occ+obj 75.21/64.79, obj+room 74.03/63.51, occ+room 74.97/64.66, all 75.80/65.37 (mIoU 12.93, mAP 33.57, layout IoU 66.45)
findings.relevance: Justifies an occupancy-prediction auxiliary loss on Model A's LiDAR/BEV tokens.

findings.claim: A binaural spatial-audio encoder (mel + interaural phase difference, 10 s at 32 kHz, 16x16 patches into a 12-layer transformer with three [CLS] tokens for class, distance and direction) reaches 17.94-degree mean angular error and 50.03 mAP, and its output tokens linearly projected into LLaMA-2 7B answer spatial-sound questions at 76.89%.
findings.source_title: BAT: Learning to Reason about Spatial Sounds with Large Language Models
findings.kind: ICML 2024 paper (arXiv PDF read via local pdftotext), CC BY 4.0
findings.numbers: Input (4,1024,128) = 2 mel + cos/sin IPD; window 1024, hop 320, 128 mel; 16x16 patches (64x8=512 tokens computed from stated dims, 25% masked in training) + 3 CLS; mAP 50.03%, MAE 17.94 deg, DER within 0.5 m 32.54%, ER20 23.89; SELDnet 42.66/25.19/19.21; QA 76.89%; SpatialSoundQA rendered with SoundSpaces 2.0 in Matterport3D
findings.relevance: Provides the 'audio event token' shape (class/distance/direction) for Model A's stream, though it is binaural not 4-mic array.

findings.claim: SoundSpaces 2.0 renders geometry-based binaural/ambisonic audio fast enough for RL (33.5 FPS high-speed mode at 9.5% RT60 error), an agent trained on it keeps SPL 49.3 vs 27.5 for a SoundSpaces-1.0 agent in continuous space, and its RIRs fine-tune far-field ASR to WER 12.48 - better than real IR sets (13.32).
findings.source_title: SoundSpaces 2.0: A Simulation Platform for Visual-Acoustic Learning
findings.kind: NeurIPS 2022 Datasets and Benchmarks paper (arXiv PDF read via local pdftotext); code github.com/facebookresearch/sound-spaces
findings.numbers: Xeon Gold 6230: high-quality 0.9/4.0 FPS (1/5 threads), high-speed 7.7/33.5 FPS, RT60 error 9.5%; DRR error 0.98 dB vs 11.0 dB (SS1); continuous nav: SS1-trained 64.2% SR/27.5% SPL (0.9% with continuous sound), SS2-trained 64.7%/49.3%/DTG 5.9 m; ASR WER: pretrained 29.10, real IRs 13.32, Pyroomacoustics 16.24, SS1 18.48, SS2 12.48; mono/binaural/ambisonic outputs, configurable mics
findings.relevance: The desktop simulator for training Parcel's audio branch and array-specific DoA tokens.

findings.claim: Long-horizon multi-goal audio-visual-language navigation is unsolved: on a 156,550-episode Matterport3D benchmark with SoundSpaces 2.0 audio and 2-4 heterogeneous goals, every learned or training-free baseline scores at most 6.0% success.
findings.source_title: LH-AVLN: A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Audio-Visual-Language Navigation
findings.kind: arXiv preprint (full text read at arxiv.org/html/2607.03920), CC BY 4.0
findings.numbers: 156,550 episodes, 550 validation; ordered/unordered SR: MTU3D 1.7/2.1, 3D-Mem 0.0/1.0, SAVi 0.0/0.0, GOAT-Bench 0.0/0.2, PAG-Nav 2.3/3.1, MAV-Nav (SAVN-CE transformer + frozen CLIP ViT-B/32 + CNN binaural encoder) 2.2/6.0; 1.0 m sensor height; no LLM/VLM agent evaluated
findings.relevance: Scopes Parcel's audio behaviours to single-goal events sequenced by the plan lane.

findings.claim: On the one 2026 vision-language navigation system deployed on a Unitree quadruped with a Mid-360 LiDAR, D455 and Jetson Orin NX, the LiDAR map is used only for SLAM pose and frontier scoring and is never passed to the VLM as an image or tokens; real-world success is 95% for large and 65% for small objects.
findings.source_title: A Deployable Embodied Vision-Language Navigation System with Hierarchical Cognition and Context-Aware Exploration (HiCo-Nav)
findings.kind: arXiv preprint (full text read at arxiv.org/html/2604.21363v1)
findings.numbers: Qwen3-Omni API online or local Qwen3-VL-8B; YOLO-World, Mobile-SAM, CLIP; sim SR/SPL MP3D 48.5/21.5, HM3D 61.0/31.8, HM3D-OVON 52.4/20.7, TextNav 27.8/12.9; real 40 episodes: 95% large, 65% small; 0.22 s per frame, 1.54 m/s, 21.5 s mean task time
findings.relevance: The modular alternative on Parcel-class hardware: LiDAR stays in the classical stack while the VLM sees keyframes and objects.

design_implications: Put the Mid-360 into Model A's 10 Hz act-token loop as LiDAR tokens (REASAN-style 30x180 ray image or ViLiNT-style polar-grid tokens, tens to a few hundred tokens), not as text and not through the VLM: the only measured navigation transformer with LiDAR tokens loses ~50% SR when they are masked, and the same encoder shape runs at 50 Hz in ~1.3 ms on Parcel's exact Go2 / Mid-360 / Orin stack.

Give the 0.5-2 Hz language/plan lane the occupancy grid as ONE annotated image (labels at region centroids, a coordinate grid, trajectory and pose drawn in), because raw obstacle maps are worth ~0 SR to a VLM (MapNav 27.3 -> 26.4; TopV-Nav +3) while labels/coordinates are worth +7-10 SR; this costs one frame's tokens (NavFoM: 64) and constant memory (MapNav: 0.17 MB).

If occupancy ever enters the trained policy as tokens, budget 11x11 to 21x21 cells at 0.5 m (121-441 tokens; 31x31 is flat for 2x FLOPs per BEVBert), use egocentric relative coordinates (GridMM), and add an occupancy-prediction auxiliary head (VER: +2-3 SR).

Encode structured state as one MLP token per vector plus identifier tokens: goal bearing/distance -> 1 token with a NoMaD-style goal mask for 'no goal / owner said stop'; plan state (sub-goal id, step, paused) -> 1 token; camera azimuth and time -> NavFoM sinusoidal identifier tokens; candidate targets from the plan lane -> FOM-Nav per-entity tokens (MLP(coords)+MLP(geodesic dist)+visual+CLIP-text+type) within ~200 tokens.

Audio events should reach the act-token loop as a low-rate bearing/distance/class token (BAT's three [CLS] outputs, ~18-degree DoA) or a small local sound-field grid (Sim2Real-AVN 9x9), not as raw audio: the only real-robot audio-nav transfer (75%, 20 trials) used field prediction + planner and the end-to-end RL policy scored 0% in the real world.

Every audio-nav encoder found is binaural/HRTF; Parcel's XVF3800 is a 4-mic array, so either tokenize the array's own beamformer DoA as a bearing, or retrain the audio branch on SoundSpaces 2.0 audio rendered with the array's mic configuration (supported; 33.5 FPS high-speed mode).

Model B should keep the owner's voice, not only ASR text: speech tokens (~300 Whisper tokens per utterance) beat an ASR cascade by 5-18 points on chained tasks, and speaker-conditioned retrieval lifts owner-specific tasks from 19% to 86% (VLAS); emit the steering injection as a structured constraint token (adverbs, exclusions) that the 10 Hz loop consumes, and build narration receipts from the same plan-state token so Model A and Model B cannot drift.

Scope companion audio behaviours as single-goal events sequenced by the plan lane; multi-goal audio-visual-language missions are at <= 6% SR for every published method (LH-AVLN), and even map-retrieval sound goals fall from 60-75% (one goal) to 7-33% (four in a row) (AVLMaps).

Keep a modular fallback in the design: the one 2026 Mid-360 quadruped VLN system (HiCo-Nav, Orin NX) reaches 95%/65% real success with LiDAR used only for SLAM and frontier scoring, never entering the VLM.

Open gaps to price into the plan: no published quadruped language-navigation VLA consumes LiDAR occupancy tokens; no published navigation policy tokenizes user identity/preferences (VLAS Voice RAG is the nearest analogue, in manipulation); no navigation policy consumes a microphone array.
